title: 第二十四章第二十五章第二十六章
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
开春的时候，蒙训院来了新生。
说是新生，其实也不算新——这批人跟苏尘一样，都是满十五岁才来入学的。只是苏尘他们去年秋天就来了，这批是赶着开春补报的，前后差了半年。要么是家里有事没来得及报到的，被府衙上门催促了，要么是别的城转学过来的，大概就是这么些人。
消息是文师在早课前说的。他说完以后，底下十几个人反应不大——无非是多了一批人一起上课，该跑圈还是跑圈，该抄书还是抄书。但文师后续又补了一句：新生要分班，人数凑够一班的量，所以要重新分。
这一句让学堂里安静了一拍。
苏尘坐在最后一排靠窗的位置，手里转着一支秃了尖的毛笔，听完没什么表情。重新分班对他没什么影响——他在哪个班都是混。
他旁边的阿离倒是抬了一下头，看了文师一眼，然后低下头继续抄她的功课。半年下来，她的字已经不像最初那样歪歪扭扭了，笔画稳了，间距也匀了，虽然算不上好看，但至少看得出是认真写的。
文师把分班名单念了一遍。
苏尘被分在甲班，阿离在乙班。两个人的位置隔了一排。
念完名字，文师合上名册，补了一句：新生下周一报到。这几天先各自把位子腾一腾。
下课后，阿离收拾书袋的动作比平时快了一些。苏尘靠在窗边，看她把笔和纸一样一样往袋子里塞，塞到一半停了下来，想了想，又把笔抽出来重新摆了一遍。
她没有说话，但他看得出来她在调整情绪。
甲班和乙班，各占学堂的左右两半。隔了一排课桌，不碍事。
但苏尘知道她不是在想这个——她在想的是：新的教室里会坐满她不认识的人。
他没说什么。把书袋往肩上一搭，走了出去。
阿离跟上来，两个人一前一后穿过院子。
院子里的槐树已经抽了新芽，嫩绿嫩绿的，跟去年秋天满树枯黄的样子完全不同。春风从巷子口灌进来，带着泥土和青草的气味。
阿离走在他身侧，说了一句：“下周一分班了。”
“嗯。”
“新生里有你认识的吗？”
“一个人都不认识。”苏尘说。

阿离想了想，似乎觉得这个答案挺合理，就没再问了。
周一，新生入学的日子。
苏尘到学堂的时候，院子里已经站了七八个人。有男有女，年纪都在十五上下，穿着各自从家里带来的衣裳——有粗布的，有细棉的，还有两个穿着半新的锦缎料子，应该是城中富户家的孩子。
文师站在院门口，手里拿着一张新名册，正在对着人打勾。
苏尘扫了一眼那排新生。
第一眼看过去，没什么特别的。
第二眼的时候，他注意到队伍末尾站着的一个女孩。
她站在靠墙的位置，跟旁边的人隔了半个身位。穿了一件灰蓝色的旧布衫，袖口洗得有点发白，但干干净净。头发用一根暗红色的布条在脑后扎成一条辫子，垂到腰侧。她的脸不算白——不是晒出来的那种肤色，更像是一种天生的冷白，在院子里灰扑扑的色调里显得不太搭。
她没在跟旁边的人说话，而是东张西望，像是在找人。
苏尘多看了她一眼。
他的眼光在判断一个人是否练过功的时候几乎不会出错——这个女孩的站姿不一样。她重心压得比一般人低，双脚微微分开，肩膀放松但不前倾，是一种长期保持警觉后养成的体态习惯。站过桩的人才会有这种站法。
武师出身的家庭，或者——她自己练过。
文师点完了名，带着新生往学堂这边走。那女孩跟队伍一起移动，步伐很稳，落地的节奏均匀，不是那种走快了就会晃的打法。
苏尘进了学堂，在自己的位置上坐下来。甲班在左边，乙班在右边。新生分到哪个班的都有，按名单坐。
那个灰蓝布衫的女孩被分到了甲班，坐在苏尘斜前方隔了两排的位置上。
文师站在讲台上，先让新生一个一个起来做了自我介绍。轮到那女孩的时候，她站起来，声音不大，但很清楚：
“陶夭夭。朔州本地人，家中从商。”
说完就坐下了。没有多余的话，没有紧张地抿嘴，也没有刻意笑得自然。
苏尘靠在椅背上，看了一眼她的背影。她说“从商“的时候语气很平——不是在撒谎的那种平，是准备好了台词的那种平。
开学第一天的课没什么特别的。文师讲了一节经义，又发了一篇短文让抄写。武课因为新生入学临时取消了，改成统一发基础功法的册子。

苏尘注意到陶夭夭拿到功法册子的时候，翻了几页，表情没什么变化。但她翻页的动作很快——不像一个从没接触过功法的人在逐字阅读，更像是在确认这跟她知道的东西是不是一样。
他收回了目光。
content_en:
At the beginning of spring, new students arrived at the Mentoring Academy.
Although they are said to be freshmen, they are not really new at all - this group of people, like Su Chen, only came to school when they were fifteen years old. It's just that Su Chen and the others came last fall, and this batch was rushed to make up for the spring application, which was half a year behind. Either they had something to do at home and didn't have time to report, so the government came to urge them, or they were transfer students from other cities, that's probably what happened.
The news was told by the literary teacher before morning class. After he finished speaking, there was little reaction from the dozen or so people below - it was just that there was an extra group of people attending class together, whether they should run laps or laps, and whether they should copy books or books. But the literary teacher then added: Freshmen need to be divided into classes, and the number of students is enough to fill one class, so they need to be divided again.
This sentence made the school quiet for a moment.
Su Chen sat in the last row by the window, spinning a bald-tip brush in his hand, and showed no expression after listening. The reclassification had no effect on him - he was mixed in every class.
A Li next to him raised his head, glanced at the writer, then lowered his head and continued copying her homework. After half a year, her handwriting is no longer as crooked as it was at first. The strokes are steady and the spacing is even. Although it is not beautiful, at least it can be seen that she wrote seriously.
The literary teacher read out the class list.
Su Chen was assigned to Class A, and A Li was in Class B. The two people are one row apart.
After reading the names, the literary teacher closed the roster and added: Freshmen will report next Monday. Let's clear up our seats for the next few days.
After class, A Li packed his book bag a little faster than usual. Su Chen leaned against the window and watched her put the pen and paper into the bag. She stopped halfway, thought for a while, took out the pen and arranged it again.
She didn't speak, but he could tell she was adjusting her emotions.
Class A and Class B each occupy the left and right halves of the school. There is a row of desks separated, so it doesn't get in the way.
But Su Chen knew that wasn't what she was thinking about - what she was thinking about was that the new classroom would be filled with people she didn't know.
He said nothing. He put his book bag on his shoulders and walked out.
A Li followed, and the two of them crossed the yard one after the other.
The locust tree in the yard has sprouted new buds, which are tender and green, completely different from last autumn when the trees were all withered and yellow. The spring breeze flows in from the entrance of the alley, carrying the smell of earth and grass.
Ah Li walked beside him and said, "We will be divided into different classes next week."
"Yeah."
"Do you know any of the freshmen?"
"I don't know anyone." Su Chen said.
Ah Li thought for a while and seemed to think the answer was quite reasonable, so he didn't ask any more questions.
Monday is the day for new students to enroll.
When Su Chen arrived at the school, seven or eight people were already standing in the courtyard. There were men and women, all around fifteen years old, wearing clothes that they had brought from home - some were made of coarse cloth, some were made of fine cotton, and two were wearing used brocade material. They should be children from wealthy families in the city.
The literary master stood at the entrance of the courtyard, holding a new roster in his hand and checking people's boxes.
Su Chen glanced at the row of freshmen.
At first glance, there's nothing special about it.
At the second glance, he noticed a girl standing at the end of the line.
She stood against the wall, half a body away from the person next to her. He was wearing an old gray-blue cloth shirt. The cuffs were a little white after washing, but they were clean. Her hair was tied into a braid at the back of her head with a dark red strip of cloth, hanging down to her waist. Her face is not white—not the kind of skin that comes out of the sun, more like a natural cold white that doesn’t match the gray tones in the yard.
She wasn't talking to the people next to her, but was looking around as if looking for someone.
Su Chen glanced at her one more time.
His eyes were almost unmistakable when it came to judging whether a person had practiced Kung Fu - this girl's stance was different. Her center of gravity is lower than that of ordinary people, her feet are slightly apart, and her shoulders are relaxed but not leaning forward. This is a way to maintain alertness for a long time.Developed body habits. Only those who have stood on piles will know how to stand like this.
She comes from a family of martial arts masters, or she has practiced it herself.
The literary teacher finished taking the roll and led the new students towards the school. The girl moved with the team, her pace was very steady, and her landing rhythm was even. She was not the kind of player who would wobble when she walked too fast.
Su Chen entered the school and sat down in his seat. Class A is on the left and Class B is on the right. Freshmen are assigned to whatever class they are assigned to, and they sit according to the list.
The girl in the gray and blue shirt was assigned to Class A and sat two rows away from Su Chen.
The literary teacher stood on the podium and first asked the freshmen to stand up one by one and introduce themselves. When it was the girl's turn, she stood up and spoke quietly but clearly:
"Tao Yaoyao. A native of Shuozhou, his family is engaged in business."
After saying that, he sat down. There were no unnecessary words, no nervous pursed lips, and no deliberate smiles.
Su Chen leaned back on the chair and glanced at her back. When she said "business", her tone was very calm - not the kind of calmness where she was lying, but the kind of calmness where she had prepared her lines.
The first day of school was nothing special. The scribe explained the meaning of a verse and then sent a short article for him to copy. Martial arts classes were temporarily canceled due to the enrollment of new students, and they were replaced by a unified distribution of basic exercise booklets.
Su Chen noticed that when Tao Yaoyao got the exercise booklet, she flipped through a few pages without any change in her expression. But she turned the pages very quickly - not like someone who had never been exposed to Kung Fu and was reading word for word, but more like she was confirming whether it was the same as what she knew.
He looked away.
